Question: In our number system the base is ten. If the base were changed to four you would count as follows: \(1,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(10,\) \(11,\) \(12,\) \(13,\) \(20,\) \(21,\) \(22,\) \(23,\) \(30,\) \(\ldots\) The twentieth number would be:
Solution:
The counting starts at one and increases by one each time, so the twentieth number represents twenty.

In base four, the rightmost places represent ones, fours, and sixteens: each place is worth four times the place to its right. Since
\[
20=1\cdot16+1\cdot4+0\cdot1,
\]
the digits are \(1,1,0\). Thus the twentieth number is \(\boxed{110}\) in base four, choice E.
